name: Toy store web analytics
story: An online toy store (Maven Fuzzy Factory) selling four stuffed-animal products. Every website session, pageview, order and refund from Mar 2012 to Mar 2015, with paid search and social campaigns.

source.title: Toy Store E-Commerce Database (Maven Fuzzy Factory)
source.credit: Maven Analytics, shared by Siddharth Vora

tables.name: dim_products
tables.description: One row per product. Four products launched between 2012 and 2014.

columns.name: pageview_seq
columns.description: Order of the pageview within its session, starting at 1

tables.name: fct_sessions
tables.description: One row per website session with traffic source, landing page, bounce and conversion.
tables.grain: One row per website session with traffic source, landing page, bounce and conversion

columns.name: is_repeat_session
columns.description: True if the visitor had an earlier session

columns.name: utm_source
columns.description: gsearch, bsearch or socialbook; null for unpaid traffic

columns.name: utm_campaign
columns.description: nonbrand, brand, pilot, desktop_targeted; null for unpaid

columns.name: http_referer
columns.description: Referring site; null for direct type-in

columns.name: channel_group
columns.description: direct, organic_search, paid_brand, paid_nonbrand, paid_social (derived from utm and referer)

columns.name: order_id
columns.description: Order placed in the session, if any

columns.name: revenue_usd
columns.description: Order revenue in USD, 0 if no order

columns.name: primary_product_id
columns.description: First product added to the cart

tables.name: fct_order_items
tables.description: One row per item in an order, with refunds.
tables.grain: One row per item in an order, with refunds

columns.name: is_primary_item
columns.description: First item added to the cart

columns.name: refunded_at
columns.description: Refund timestamp, null if not refunded

tests.test: order revenue = sum of item prices

metrics.name: revenue
metrics.description: Order revenue in USD before refunds

metrics.name: bounce_rate
metrics.description: Single-page sessions / sessions, usually by landing_page

caveats: The raw data stored missing UTM values as the text 'NULL'; the warehouse converts them to real nulls.
channel_group is derived: no utm and no referer = direct; no utm with a referer = organic_search.
Funnel pages: landing (/home or /lander-N) -> /products -> product page -> /cart -> /shipping -> /billing or /billing-2 -> /thank-you-for-your-order.
Site tests ran over time: new landers (lander-1 to lander-5), billing-2, and a cross-sell launched Sep 2013.
questions: Which channel has the best conversion rate, and how has it changed?
Build the conversion funnel for gsearch nonbrand sessions.
Which product has the highest refund rate?

playbook.q: Which channel brings the most valuable sessions?
playbook.ask: By channel_group and utm_source: sessions, conversion rate, revenue and margin per session, and the share of users who come back for a repeat session. Which channel brings the best users, not just the most?

playbook.q: Where does the purchase funnel leak most?
playbook.ask: Build the pageview funnel from landing page to /thank-you-for-your-order, split by device_type. Where is the biggest drop between steps, and how much revenue would closing the mobile gap to desktop add?

playbook.q: Do users come back on their own, and from where?
playbook.ask: For users with a repeat session: days between first and repeat session, and which channel the repeat session came from. What share of repeat revenue came through paid search, where we pay again for a user we already had?

playbook.q: Is growth from new users or repeat users?
playbook.ask: Split each month's users and revenue into new and repeat (is_repeat_session). How has the repeat share changed from 2012 to 2015? Show the stacked trend.

playbook.q: Did new products grow order value or just shift sales?
playbook.ask: Around each product launch in dim_products, compare items per order, average order value and each product's share of revenue in the 3 months before and after. Did each launch add revenue, or cannibalize existing products?
